messages.text:
Archive representative:

We’ve reviewed the pilot confidentiality schedule and need to resolve three points.

1. Subcontractor access. Our external color specialist will need access to uncropped master images for the first batch to calibrate color accurately. We propose the specialist be named, sign the same confidentiality terms as our staff, and access files only through our secure system during the correction window. If you prefer not to release master images, we can supply 30 reference crops per batch instead, but calibration accuracy will suffer and may require a second pass.

2. Retention and deletion schedule. We need ten days after scanning to complete corrections. Proposed schedule:
- Days 0–10: master files and derivatives accessible to project staff and the named specialist for correction.
- Days 11–45: only corrected masters and QC logs retained for verification; no further subcontractor access.
- Day 45: backups rotate; all temporary correction files and backup copies are securely deleted. No unpublished donor files retained after that, except the archive’s final deliverables.

3. Publicity. We ask for written consent to publish a single anonymized process image: cropped to equipment/hands, no donor names, no legible letter text. We can submit the exact image for pre-approval before publication if you prefer.

Can you accept master-image access for the named specialist, or should we fall back to reference crops?

Use the archive’s calibration sheet for the first batch. If the specialist still needs image references, we can approve up to 30 masked crops per batch from other collections. Two collections are excluded from specialist viewing, including crops. Archive staff will approve each reference set after checking that handwriting and identifying details are fully masked. The schedule should name the specialist, bind them to the studio’s confidentiality terms, and limit them to viewing approved references in the secure system during correction. Uncropped donor masters are outside that permission. We can accommodate a second pass within the correction window.

We propose the following additional terms for signature.

- **Retention and deletion.** The correction window ends ten calendar days after each batch is scanned. By day 10, deliver the corrected masters to the archive, revoke specialist access, and securely delete all studio and specialist copies of donor files, including temporary files, derivatives and backups. The studio may retain QC logs that contain no donor content or identifying details. Within two business days of deletion, send written confirmation identifying the batch, deletion date and systems covered, including backups.
- **Incidents.** List a named incident contact, monitored email address and phone number for each party. The studio must notify the archive contact promptly, and within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, even if the investigation is ongoing.
- **Publicity.** The archive will consider one photograph of equipment alone, with hands, donor materials and screen content out of frame. Publication requires prior written approval of the exact photograph, caption and intended use. Signing the schedule grants no publication consent.

The outstanding exception is the proposed day-45 backup rotation. Can you keep pilot files out of that cycle or purge them by day 10? If neither is feasible, please identify exactly what would remain in backup, who could restore it and the earliest deletion date so we can decide that exception before signing.

Archive representative:

We withdraw the master-image access request. We accept the calibration sheet plus up to 30 masked crops from approved non-excluded collections, with the specialist named, bound to our confidentiality terms, and limited to viewing approved references in the secure system during correction. No uncropped donor masters.

To make the ten-day window workable, we ask that archive staff approve each reference set within one business day. If approval is delayed, the correction deadline should extend by the same number of days. We accept the possibility of a second pass within that window.

Retention and deletion: We accept deletion of active, temporary, derivative and specialist-accessible copies by day 10, delivery of corrected masters by day 10, and written deletion confirmation within two business days. QC logs will contain no donor content.

Backup rotation is the one exception. We cannot purge pilot files from backup by day 10. Our standard backup system retains encrypted copies for 45 days. What would remain is the encrypted backup set containing donor files, temporary files, derivatives and correction work from the batch. Restoration is restricted to two named senior studio staff with two-person authorization, and only for incident response or archive instruction. The earliest automatic deletion date is 45 days after the batch is scanned. We will send a second written confirmation once that deletion occurs.

If day-45 backup retention is unacceptable, we can implement a one-time exclusion for this pilot so donor files never enter the backup system. The tradeoff is that there would be no recovery copy during the ten-day correction window. Please indicate whether you prefer the day-45 encrypted-backup exception or the backup exclusion.

Incidents: Accepted. We will provide a named contact, monitored email address and phone number, and will notify within 24 hours of discovery.

Publicity: Accepted. We will submit the exact equipment-only photograph, caption and intended use for prior written approval. No hands, donor materials or screen content will appear.

Please confirm which backup option you want us to include in the signed schedule.

Please include the **pilot backup exclusion** in the signed schedule. Apply it before the first scan to all donor files, including temporary files, derivatives and correction work. The archive accepts the risk that a batch may need rescanning if working files are lost. Each batch’s deletion confirmation should identify the systems covered and confirm that the batch stayed out of backup. This resolves the day-45 exception.

We agree to review each reference set within one business day of receipt and return either written approval or masking corrections. The specialist may view a set only after written approval. If our response is late, please flag the affected batch promptly. We propose keeping its day-10 delivery, access cutoff and deletion deadline unless both parties agree in writing, before that deadline, to a revised date for that batch. The backup exclusion applies throughout any extension.

The batch-specific extension provision is the only point awaiting your agreement. Please carry the agreed specialist access, deletion evidence, incident notification and equipment-photograph terms into the schedule and include the specialist’s name and both parties’ incident contact details before signature.

We propose that the studio handle calibration and corrections, and that the archive conservator validate color and give final written approval. The specialist may use the calibration sheet and an archive-approved masked image of a nonrestricted comparison sheet. If masking obscures a color needed for calibration, we can arrange supervised review of the comparison original at the archive one morning next week. Only the masked version may leave the archive. Donor letters and their images, including crops, are outside the specialist’s access.

Calibration scans can proceed once the pilot backup exclusion is in place. Please send the comparison scan to the conservator for review against the original. We propose starting donor scanning once the conservator approves the calibration in writing. The conservator will also assess the corrected donor masters directly.

For each donor batch, the studio will deliver the corrected masters, end specialist access for that batch and delete all pilot working copies by day 10 after scanning. Please delete any separate calibration working files within ten calendar days of the calibration scan. The agreed backup exclusion and written deletion confirmation within two business days apply to both. A second pass or pending color review extends a deadline only if both parties agree in writing before it expires.

Can the studio validate its settings using the masked comparison image and submit a scan for the conservator’s approval, or does the specialist need the supervised morning review before donor scanning begins?

Archive representative:

We accept the overall division: studio handles calibration and corrections, conservator validates color and gives final written approval. We also accept that only the masked comparison version may leave the archive, and that donor letters and donor images, including crops, remain outside the specialist’s access.

However, the masked comparison image is not sufficient. In our first test, masking obscured an ink-tone feature the specialist needs to verify color response. We request the supervised morning review of the nonrestricted comparison original at the archive next week. The specialist will use that session only to confirm the critical ink-tone response, after which we can rely on the calibration sheet and the masked comparison image for settings. The original will not leave the archive.

We will then submit a comparison scan to the conservator for review and wait for written approval before starting donor scanning.

On deletion, we accept day-10 deletion for donor batch working copies, with the operator’s rescan acceptance test completed before deletion. If that test requires a second pass, we will request a written extension before the day-10 deadline.

For calibration working files, we ask to align deletion with approval, not the scan date. Proposed: retain calibration working files until the conservator gives written approval of the calibration, then delete within two business days and confirm deletion in writing. If approval is not received by ten calendar days after the calibration scan, we will request a written extension before that deadline. The backup exclusion applies to calibration files throughout.

Can you confirm the supervised morning review and the calibration-file deletion trigger?

We confirm the supervised morning review at the archive next week. Please send the named specialist’s availability so we can fix the morning with the conservator. The specialist may inspect the comparison original for the ink-tone check. Only the approved masked version may be copied or taken off-site. Donor letters and their images, including crops, remain outside the specialist’s access.

We accept approval as the calibration-file deletion trigger, with a day-10 limit. Delete calibration working files **within two business days after written calibration approval or by day 10 after the calibration scan, whichever comes first**. If more time is needed, both parties must agree in writing to a revised deadline before day 10 expires. The backup exclusion applies throughout. Within two business days after deletion, send written confirmation identifying the systems covered and confirming the files stayed out of backup.

Calibration scanning may proceed once the backup exclusion is in place. After the supervised check, submit the comparison scan to the conservator. Donor scanning may begin when the conservator approves calibration in writing. The studio operator will complete the rescan acceptance test, and the conservator will give final color approval for the corrected donor masters. Delivery, access cutoff and deletion of donor-batch working copies remain due by day 10 after each batch is scanned unless both parties agree in writing to a revised date before the deadline.

Archive representative:

We accept the calibration-file deletion trigger as written: delete calibration working files within two business days after written calibration approval or by day 10 after the calibration scan, whichever comes first, unless both parties agree in writing to a revised deadline before day 10 expires. The backup exclusion applies throughout. We will send written deletion confirmation within two business days, identifying systems covered and confirming the files stayed out of backup.

We confirm the sequence: backup exclusion in place before calibration scanning; supervised morning review with conservator; comparison scan submitted to conservator; donor scanning begins only after conservator’s written calibration approval; studio operator completes rescan acceptance test; conservator gives final color approval for corrected donor masters.

Named specialist availability for the supervised morning review: next Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday, starting 9:00 a.m. Please tell us which date works and we will fix the morning.

The specialist may inspect the comparison original on-site. Only the approved masked version may be copied or taken off-site. No donor letters, donor images, or crops will be accessed.

Please pencil in Tuesday, 1 December, at 9:00 a.m. local time at the archive for the supervised ink-tone review. We’ll confirm once the conservator verifies availability. The appointment is the only open item.
We will hold Tuesday, 1 December at 9:00 a.m. local time at the archive for the supervised ink-tone review, pending your confirmation once the conservator verifies availability.
